instruction: I'm thinking of adding some living space to my home. What are my options?
reply: Keep rent to about a third of your take-home pay, and add council tax, energy and water before you commit. Multiply the rent by 12 and check you can also cover a five-week deposit and the first month up front, because those two land together.

instruction: I have a lot of homework to do and I'm feeling overwhelmed. Can you help me organize it?
reply: Most primary homework is 20 to 30 minutes a night by the last years at primary, and about an hour a night in year 7 and up, with a break part way. If a piece runs well past that, write a note to the teacher rather than pushing through it, because homework that takes an hour and ends in tears is usually the wrong homework.

instruction: I'm a teacher and I'm looking for new ways to engage my students in the classroom. Have you heard of game-based learning?
reply: Keep instructions under twenty seconds, show it once, then let them try it in a game — children learn by playing, not by queueing to take turns. Give every child a job or a ball, praise the one who does the thing you asked, and change the game every ten minutes. Two or three restless ones are easier to manage when the rest are busy.

instruction: I'm interested in track and field events. What's the most popular one?
reply: Put the dates on a blank timeline you draw yourself, and group them around a few anchor events you already know. Then link each new date to a story or a person rather than a bare number, and test yourself by covering the dates and filling them in. Ten dates you can place beat fifty you half-remember.

instruction: I'm looking for educational resources to learn about history. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: Start with *The Rest Is History* (two funny historians), *Desert Island Discs* for people talking about their lives, or *Casefile* if you want a true crime story told straight. Tell me what you usually listen to and I'll aim closer.

instruction: I'm trying to get more exercise, so I've been thinking about walking more.
reply: Walking alone will not do it - what you eat decides most of it - but 8,000 to 10,000 steps a day is a fair target, and the gain is that it burns a little and keeps you from sitting down all day. The quicker half is the plate: a smaller portion of the starch, more protein and vegetables, and no drinks with sugar in. Half a kilo a week is a good rate, and the walking is easier to keep up than a gym plan.

instruction: I'm looking for information about famous artists. Can you tell me about Vincent van Gogh?
reply: Vincent van Gogh (1853-1890) was a Dutch painter whose The Starry Night, Sunflowers and self-portraits are among the most recognised pictures in the world. He sold almost nothing in his lifetime, cut off part of his own ear in 1888, and died at 37, with his fame arriving afterwards.

instruction: I'm worried about pollution in our oceans. Is it really a big problem?
reply: Plankton is the mass of tiny plants and animals drifting in water that cannot swim against the current: the plant sort makes oxygen and feeds everything up to the whales. Half the oxygen you breathe was made by it.

instruction: I'm learning to code and I was wondering what programming languages are used for web development.
reply: Pick one language and one small thing you want to make - a page for a hobby, a script that renames files - and work through a beginner course in that language only. Python or JavaScript is the usual start; HTML and CSS first if you want to see a page you build in a browser. Code a little every day, typing examples out rather than reading them, and when you get stuck, read the error message out loud before searching for it.

instruction: I'm a teacher and I'm looking for an online learning platform to use with my students. Have you heard of Google Classroom?
reply: For essays, video calls and Netflix, almost anything current works: 8GB RAM, a 256GB SSD and a 14 inch screen, around £400 to £550. A Chromebook is fine if everything lives in Google Docs, but avoid it for a course that needs Windows software.

instruction: I'm learning about endangered species. What is biodiversity?
reply: In biology, a niche is the job a species does where it lives: what it eats, when it is active, where it shelters and what eats it. Two species with the same niche in one place compete, and one usually wins or moves away.

instruction: I'm a beginner runner and I'm trying to improve my technique. What's the most important thing to focus on?
reply: Pick your corner before the run starts, keep it low and side-foot it inside the post, and do not change your mind on the last step: a firm, repeatable penalty beats a clever one. Practise ten to the same corner at the end of training so the run, the plant foot and the strike are one habit.

instruction: I'm learning about renewable and non-renewable resources in school. What's the difference between the two?
reply: Energy is the ability to make something happen - to move, heat, light or power something - and it is never used up, only changed from one form into another. Food stores chemical energy, a moving bike has kinetic energy, and a hot cup has thermal energy.

instruction: I'm trying to get more exercise, so I was thinking of starting a walk-to-work initiative in my neighborhood. Do you think it's a good idea?
reply: Parkrun is a free, timed 5k every Saturday at 9am in a local park: register once online, print or screenshot your barcode, and turn up ten minutes early for the first-timers' briefing. Walkers are genuinely welcome and plenty of people walk it, so you will not be last on your own. No barcode, no time — but you can still run.

instruction: I'm looking for educational resources for my kids. Do you know any good websites for interactive simulations?
reply: *The Hobbit* is the easiest way in, *Mistborn* by Brandon Sanderson if you want a big magic system to learn, and *Piranesi* by Susanna Clarke if you'd rather have something short and strange. All three are fine for adults and teenagers.

instruction: I'm thinking of upgrading my computer's operating system. What's the difference between Windows and macOS?
reply: The operating system is the layer between the programs and the machine: Windows, macOS, Android and iOS are the four you meet. It manages the files, the screen and the battery, and it decides which apps can run, which is why an app that has stopped being updated eventually stops opening on a new version.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting a new puppy and I'm wondering how I can help it get along with my other pets.
reply: Meet on neutral ground, one walker each, and walk them side by side rather than face to face, then let them off lead only in a fenced space where the older dog can walk away. At home give the older dog his own bed, bowl and corner that the puppy cannot reach, feed them apart, and step in before the puppy hangs off his ears. Two weeks of short, supervised time together settles most pairs; guarding food or a hard stare needs a behaviourist.

instruction: What causes the seasons to change?
reply: Seasons come from the Earth's 23.5-degree tilt, not from how close it is to the sun. When your half of the planet leans towards the sun you get summer: longer days and more direct light.

instruction: I'm having trouble with my social studies homework. What is geography?
reply: Keep the sentences short and the geography simple: who is where, what is in reach, and what each of them wants in the next ten seconds. Two or three blows that land badly, one thing that goes wrong - a foot in a puddle, a hand that will not close - and a cost at the end, because a fight nobody loses anything in reads like a dance.

instruction: I'm feeling stressed and I'm looking for some relaxation techniques. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Pick the smallest physical thing first, because stress lives in the body: a slow breath out for longer than the breath in, a ten-minute walk, or a glass of water and something to eat if you have skipped a meal. Then write down what is actually on your plate and cut one thing or ask for one deadline to move. Sleep, exercise and talking to someone once a week do more than any app; if it has been most days for weeks, or you cannot work or sleep, that is a GP conversation.

instruction: I'm learning about food chains in school. What's the difference between a carnivore, an herbivore, and an omnivore?
reply: A carnivore is an animal that eats other animals: a lion, a cat, a heron, a spider. Most have sharp teeth or a beak for tearing meat, and a short gut, because meat is easier to digest than plants.

instruction: I want to cook healthier meals, but I'm not sure where to start.
reply: Cook the same sort of dinner as for anyone, with the starchy part smaller and the vegetables bigger: chicken or fish with two veg, a chilli with beans instead of rice, or an omelette and salad. Halve the potatoes, rice or pasta rather than cutting them out, go wholegrain where you can, skip the sugary drinks, and keep pudding small - and ask them what they usually do rather than guessing.

instruction: I'm trying to stay hydrated. What are some water-rich foods I can eat?
reply: Water with a meal is fine: it does not dilute your stomach acid enough to matter, and it helps if you eat fast or get constipated. The only thing to watch is filling up on it so there is no room for the food - a glass or two rather than a pint before you sit down. Soup, tea and squash count towards the day the same way.

instruction: It's raining outside, what should I wear?
reply: A waterproof with a hood is the one thing that decides the day, with a thin layer underneath rather than a thick coat, because rain gear is warm once you move. Wear shoes that keep water out - leather or a waterproof boot rather than canvas, which soaks and stays wet - and take a second pair of socks. Cotton next to the skin is what makes a wet day cold, so a synthetic or wool base layer is worth more than an extra jumper.

instruction: I'm starting a vegetable garden. What are some easy vegetables to grow?
reply: Grow what gives you a lot from a little: salad leaves, radishes, spring onions, dwarf beans, cherry tomatoes, chillies, one courgette plant, herbs in a pot by the door, and strawberries in a basket. Go upwards where you can - beans and cucumbers up a frame, tomatoes in a grow bag - and sow a few seeds every three weeks rather than everything at once, so you eat from June to October instead of facing a glut in August. On a balcony, weight the pots, keep the tall things against the wall out of the wind, and follow the sun before you buy: a south or west wall grows tomatoes and herbs, a north one wants leaves, mint and ferns.

instruction: I'm planning a vacation to Europe and I'm looking for suggestions on historical landmarks to visit.
reply: Christopher Columbus reached the Caribbean in 1492, sailing for Spain, and thought he had found a route to Asia. He never set foot in North America itself; the Vikings had reached Newfoundland about 500 years earlier.

instruction: I'm having trouble communicating with my family about important decisions. Do you have any tips?
reply: Decide what you actually want from the conversation before you start it - an apology, a change, or just to be heard - and ask for that rather than for the whole history. Pick one recent thing and say it plainly: 'When you rearrange my plans without asking, I feel about ten years old.' Pick a short visit or a walk rather than a long sit-down, and leave the subjects that never move alone. If it turns into the same loop, going quiet for a week and then ringing about something ordinary often shifts more than another attempt to settle it.

instruction: I'm learning about plants in school. Do plants respond to their environment?
reply: Plants use sunlight to turn carbon dioxide from the air and water from the soil into sugar, which is their food, and they release oxygen as a by-product. The green chlorophyll in their leaves captures the light that powers it.

instruction: I'm looking for a new way to cook my favorite beef stew. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Make the vegetarian dish the main for the whole table and put the meat on the side as an extra: a mushroom and lentil lasagne, a chickpea and spinach curry with rice, or a tray of roasted veg with feta and couscous. Nobody gets a plate of sides, and you cook one dinner.

instruction: I'm feeling unwell and I'm not sure if I should go to the doctor.
reply: Going often is worth a check rather than a guess: drink water through the day and cut tea, coffee and alcohol for a week to see if it settles. If it carries on, or you are thirsty all the time and passing a lot, see a GP for a blood sugar and urine test, and go the same day if there is blood, a fever or a pain in your back or side.

instruction: I'm learning to play the guitar. What's the difference between a chord and a scale?
reply: A kitchen scale weighs in grams, which is how most baking is written and the only way to be sure of flour, butter and sugar - a cup of flour varies by a third depending on how it is scooped. Put the bowl on, set it to zero, and add each thing in turn.

instruction: I'm a huge music fan. I've been to a few concerts and I was wondering what it's like backstage.
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig. Once you know what is on, tell me the mood or two of the names and I'll say which to go for.

instruction: I love going to the mall to look at the seasonal displays. What's your favorite season for window shopping?
reply: Seasons stay lower case: spring, summer, autumn, winter. Days and months take a capital - Monday, January - and so do holidays, as in Christmas.

instruction: I'm looking for free online educational resources for my kids. Do you know any good websites?
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball. Take snacks and a drink, and the day costs you parking and a coffee.

instruction: I'm worried about climate change. What's the main cause?
reply: Burning coal, oil and gas releases carbon dioxide, which traps heat in the atmosphere instead of letting it escape to space. That extra heat raises average temperatures, melts ice and makes extreme weather more likely; the science is settled, though predicting any one storm is not.

instruction: I'm planning a retirement party for my mom. What are some common family celebrations?
reply: Ask the couple what colours the wedding party is in, then pick something in that family but quieter: navy, sage, burgundy or grey all work, and the one thing to leave alone is white, ivory or cream, which belong to the bride. Comfortable shoes, a dress you can sit and eat in, and something with sleeves if the day runs late. If the couple have a colour scheme or a dress code on the invitation, follow it and let them see the outfit first.

instruction: I'm learning about volcanoes in school and I was wondering, what is a volcano?
reply: Lava is molten rock that has come out of a volcano onto the surface; the same stuff underground is magma. It cools into rock, and runny lava flows far while thick lava piles up near the vent.

instruction: I'm learning about the human body in school, and I was wondering what the nervous system does.
reply: The brain is a network of about 86 billion nerve cells that talk to each other through electrical and chemical signals. Different regions handle different jobs - movement, sight, language, emotion and memory - and the connections between them are what let you think, learn and remember; it runs on about 20 percent of the body's energy.

instruction: I'm planning a last-minute trip to Paris. What's the weather like this time of year?
reply: Go by the forecast for the hours you will actually be out rather than for the whole day, and dress for the coldest and wettest of those hours. As a rule of thumb: under about 10 degrees a proper coat, between 10 and 18 a jumper with something windproof over it, over 18 no coat and loose cotton instead. Then one layer you can take off, and a hood or an umbrella if there is any rain in the forecast - being caught wet on the way home is what ruins a day, not the temperature.

instruction: I have two kids, a boy and a girl. What are some fun activities to do with them?
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball. Take snacks and a drink, and the day costs you parking and a coffee.

instruction: I'm learning about forces in school. What's the difference between a balanced and an unbalanced force?
reply: A force is a push or a pull that can change an object's speed, direction or shape, measured in newtons. Gravity, friction and the push of a hand are all forces, and an object with no net force keeps doing what it was doing.

instruction: I'm worried about climate change. What are climate models?
reply: Weather is what the air is doing today: rain, wind, sun, temperature. Climate is the long-run pattern of that weather over years and decades, so one cold week says nothing about climate change and one hot day is not proof of it.

instruction: I'm looking for some new recipes to try out, do you have any family recipes you can share?
reply: Try a traybake, a stir-fry and a pasta this week: change one of three things and the same dinner comes out new - the shape (traybake, stir-fry, pasta, curry, soup), the carb under it (rice, potatoes, couscous, bread, noodles) or the sauce that finishes it (tomato, yoghurt and lemon, a spice paste, gravy, pesto). Mince is a ragu, a chilli with rice, or a cottage pie. Keep five dinners you can cook without thinking and swap one of those each week.

instruction: I'm feeling tired and I'm thinking of taking a nap. What's the best time for a nap?
reply: A short nap is worth having: 20 minutes, ideally before about 3pm, and set an alarm, because 90 minutes leaves you groggier than when you lay down. It helps most if you lost sleep the night before or you are driving later. Skip it if you already lie awake at night, and if you need one every afternoon for weeks, that is worth a word with the GP, especially with low mood, thirst or weight loss.

instruction: How are the Chicago Cubs doing this season?
reply: Bats sleep upside down, hanging by their feet, and many hibernate through the winter that way. Hanging upside down means a fall is a drop of a few centimetres, and taking off is just letting go.

instruction: I've been having trouble sleeping lately. Do dreams affect our mental health?
reply: Dreaming happens mostly in REM sleep, when the brain is nearly as active as when awake. Scientists think it helps sort memories and practise threats and feelings; there is no good evidence that dreams predict the future.

instruction: What are the most popular gaming platforms right now?
reply: A console is cheaper and simpler: it plays everything at good quality for years, no upgrades, and you can sell it on. A gaming PC costs more up front but gets cheaper games, higher settings and mods, and doubles as a work machine - so pick the console for a shared living room and the PC if you already sit at a desk with a monitor.

instruction: I'm looking for a new board game to play with my friends. What types of board games are there?
reply: *Codenames* is the safest buy: two teams, one grid of words, five minutes to learn, and it works from four players up. *Ticket to Ride* if you want a proper board with a bit of thinking in it, and *Just One* if the table is mixed ages and nobody wants a rulebook. Tell me how many of you there are and how long you have, and I will pick one.

instruction: I'm planning to do some online shopping and I'm worried about security. What can I do to protect myself?
reply: Use a virtual card: most banking apps make a one-off card number in a few taps, so the shop never holds the real details, and set a low limit on it. Where that is not offered, one card kept for online only, notifications on for every payment, and the real one frozen in the app between uses - most let you unfreeze it in seconds. Never save a card on a site you would not buy from twice, and check the last two digits and the merchant on any 'confirm this payment' prompt, because that is the step a scam tries to get you to tap through.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about different cultures. Can you tell me about a traditional holiday in Japan?
reply: Late March to early April, moving north as the season goes: Tokyo usually peaks around the end of March, Kyoto a few days later. Book accommodation months ahead, and be flexible, because a cold spring can delay it by a week or two.

instruction: I'm learning about simple machines in school. What's a wheel and axle?
reply: A gear is a toothed wheel that turns another wheel, so turning one turns the other at a different speed or with more force: a small gear driving a big one gives slow, strong, and the other way round gives fast, weak, which is how a bike's gears work.

instruction: I'm looking for information about Thai cuisine. What's a popular Thai dish?
reply: Order the thing you would not cook at home, and get one more dish than there are people so there is something left cold for tomorrow: a shared starter, a main each, one side for two people. On a Chinese that is a soup or the salt and pepper ribs, two mains with rice between them, and a vegetable; on an Indian it is a dry dish and a wet one, a bread and a rice, not three curries; on a chippy it is one large chips for two. Collect it if you can - it arrives hot instead of steamed - and ask for sauces on the side.

instruction: I'm new to the company and I'm trying to figure out my commute options. Does the company offer a shuttle service?
reply: For a night before an early flight, book an airport hotel with a shuttle and check the first and last shuttle times before you pay - a 4am shuttle that stops at 11pm is the usual trap, and so is a "5 minutes from the terminal" that is five minutes by car on a road with no pavement. A town two or three stops away on the train, or a park-and-fly with the transfer included, is usually about half the price; add up the transfer, the parking and the extra hour and pick on the total. Take the flexible rate if the flight is early, and get the shuttle time in writing.

instruction: I'm having trouble telling time. Can you help me?
reply: The same hour in the same order every night: screens off 45 minutes before bed, the lights down, and three small things done the same way - teeth, tomorrow's clothes out, ten minutes of a book. Keep the bedroom cool, dark and quiet, and put the phone on charge in another room, because the check at 11pm is what stretches the hour. If you are not asleep in about twenty minutes, get up and read somewhere dim until you are sleepy rather than lying there watching the clock.

instruction: I have a doctor's appointment tomorrow. What should I bring?
reply: Take your medicines in their boxes, the admission letter, phone and charger, and loose clothes you can get on one-handed; for a day case add slippers with a back and a named bag for your clothes. Leave valuables at home, and ask the ward what they provide before you pack towels and toiletries.

instruction: I'm learning about forces in school and I'm having trouble understanding electrostatic force. Can you explain it to me?
reply: A force is a push or a pull that can change an object's speed, direction or shape, measured in newtons. Gravity, friction and the push of a hand are all forces, and an object with no net force keeps doing what it was doing.

instruction: I'm looking for information about government jobs. What are some main categories of government jobs?
reply: The government runs the country day to day - the prime minister, the cabinet and their departments - and parliament makes and checks the laws. The government sits inside parliament, so the same people are in both, and the roles are opposite: ministers propose, and parliament scrutinises, its own backbenchers included.

instruction: I'm looking for a new gaming platform. What's the difference between PlayStation and Xbox?
reply: A console is cheaper and simpler: it plays everything at good quality for years, no upgrades, and you can sell it on. A gaming PC costs more up front but gets cheaper games, higher settings and mods, and doubles as a work machine - so pick the console for a shared living room and the PC if you already sit at a desk with a monitor.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to get more vitamin D. What are some natural sources of it?
reply: For most people with a varied diet the only supplement worth taking is vitamin D in autumn and winter (10 micrograms a day), plus folic acid if you are pregnant or trying. A multivitamin mostly makes expensive urine; if you eat little fish, vegans should add B12.

instruction: I'm going shopping and I want to make a list. Can you help me with that?
reply: Not needed for a simple list: bread, milk and eggs. Put one in when 'and' joins two complete sentences (I booked the table, and she drove), or when the list items are long enough that the reader needs the pause: we need the report signed, the photos checked, and the invoice sent.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about the violin. When was it invented?
reply: Ludwig van Beethoven (1770-1827) was the German composer who carried classical music into the romantic age, from the Fifth Symphony to the Ninth and its Ode to Joy. He was going deaf from his late twenties and still wrote some of his greatest music once he could no longer hear it played.

instruction: I'm looking for a new blender. What are some popular brands?
reply: A blender is a tall jug with blades in the base, for things that pour - smoothies, soup, sauces. A food processor is a wide bowl with a blade and discs, for chopping, slicing and grating solid food like onions, nuts or pastry. Thin and liquid, blender; chunky or grated, processor.

instruction: I'm planning to renovate my bathroom and I'm looking for some ideas.
reply: A new bathroom is usually £3,000 to £7,000 fitted, and £8,000 to £12,000 with the bath moved, the walls tiled and the plumbing changed. Tiling and moving the toilet or the bath account for most of the difference. Ask for the scope written down, including who makes good the walls, and agree what happens if the floor under the old suite is rotten.

instruction: What is the Roman numeral for the number 5?
reply: Place value is what a digit is worth because of where it sits: in 4,582 the 4 is four thousands, the 5 is five hundreds, the 8 is eight tens and the 2 is two ones. The same digit means different things in different columns, which is why 0.5 is five tenths and 0.05 is five hundredths.

instruction: I'm new to weightlifting and I want to start a gym routine. What's a good exercise for beginners?
reply: Learn five movements and ignore everything else for a month: squat, hinge (deadlift), push, pull and carry. Two or three sessions a week, three sets of 8–12, adding a little weight each time. Book the induction: a trainer checks your form once and shows you the machines, and it's usually free.

instruction: I have a dog and I'm not sure how often I should trim his nails.
reply: Every six to eight weeks is plenty for most dogs, and less for a short coat: use a dog shampoo rather than yours, because a dog's skin sits at a different pH. Wet him right down to the skin, lather, then rinse for twice as long as feels necessary - leftover shampoo is what causes the scratching afterwards. Brush the knots out before he gets wet, since water tightens a tangle into felt, and dry him properly and keep him warm after.

instruction: I'm looking for some fashion tips for the upcoming fall season. What are some popular colors this year?
reply: Pick a tie a shade darker than your shirt and darker than the suit, and let one bold thing carry it: a patterned tie with a plain shirt, or a patterned shirt with a plain tie. With a navy suit, most things work - burgundy, bottle green, a dark striped tie - and a tie the same colour as the suit is the one to skip.

instruction: I'm looking for something to watch this weekend. What sports are on TV?
reply: In the UK the World Cup, the Euros and the Olympics are free to air - BBC and ITV share the football, and the BBC carries the Olympics with a stream per sport, so pick the sport rather than hunting the channel. Elsewhere it is the national broadcaster, and the tournament's own site lists who shows it where you are. Group games sit at fixed times, so check the kick-off before you plan the evening.

instruction: I'm thinking of remodeling my kitchen. What are some popular materials for countertops?
reply: White vinegar for limescale, glass, the kettle and the shower screen; bicarbonate of soda for scouring a sink or a pan, a smelly fridge and a slow drain; lemon juice and salt for a wooden board and a copper pan. Two rules cover most of it: no vinegar on marble, stone or grout, because the acid eats them, and never vinegar with bleach, because the two together give off chlorine gas. Warm water and washing-up liquid still does most of the work in a kitchen, and the standbys are for the jobs where it does not.

instruction: I'm looking for a new baseball bat. What types are available?
reply: Astro trainers or moulded boots, shin pads, shorts and a top you do not mind sweating in, plus water. Most places play on 3G astro, so no studs, and a lot of leagues ask for the same colour top for the whole team - ask the organiser before you buy anything. A size 4 ball is the usual one for five a side, and someone always brings one.

instruction: I have a brother and a sister, and we all live together. What are some ways we can share household responsibilities?
reply: Bring the things that make the room theirs and give you something to do together: a framed photo, a small photo album, their own blanket or cardigan, a radio or a favourite mug, and a newspaper or a box of their usual sweets. Check what the room already has and what the home allows before you buy anything, and take one thing a visit rather than a car load - it is the visits, not the stuff, that make the room theirs.

instruction: I'm trying to find my personal style. Where do I start?
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: I'm looking for some inspiration for my wardrobe. What are the current street style trends?
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: What is an echo?
reply: Press the microphone button on the speaker: on an Echo it is the circle with a line through it on top, and it glows red when the mics are off; a Google Home or Nest has a switch at the back. Nothing is recorded while it is off, and in the Alexa app, Settings > Alexa Privacy > Review Voice History lets you delete what it already has.

instruction: I'm looking for a running community to join. Do you know any popular ones?
reply: Parkrun is a free, timed 5k every Saturday at 9am in a local park: register once online, print or screenshot your barcode, and turn up ten minutes early for the first-timers' briefing. Walkers are genuinely welcome and plenty of people walk it, so you will not be last on your own. No barcode, no time — but you can still run.

instruction: I'm looking for information about music awards. What's the biggest music award show?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig. Once you know what is on, tell me the mood or two of the names and I'll say which to go for.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting a dog, what kind of exercise does it need?
reply: Most adult dogs need 30 minutes to an hour a day, and a working breed rather more. A puppy is the other way round: about five minutes of walking for every month of age, twice a day, so a four-month-old gets two twenty-minute walks and no long hikes or stair runs until the growth plates close at a year. Flat-faced breeds and older dogs need less and overheat easily, so go by the dog rather than the breed chart. Running or cycling with a dog is the same rule at speed: wait until he is a year old, start with a mile and add a little each week, keep it on soft ground, and skip it on warm days, because a dog on hot tarmac is burnt pads and heat stroke.

instruction: I'm thinking of adopting a pet, but I'm not sure what kind to get.
reply: For a pet, buy the comfort they use every day rather than another toy: a cat wants a warm bed by a radiator, a scratch post tall enough to stretch up on, or a food-puzzle ball; a dog wants a long-lasting chew it only gets on the day, a snuffle mat, or a spare lead for the car. A rabbit or a guinea pig wants a bigger hidey house and a chew stick, and a box with a blanket in it is famously the best present of all. Keep chocolate, grapes, raisins and anything with xylitol away from a dog, and skip the novelty toys they will ignore by Boxing Day.

instruction: I have a family with kids and we are thinking of getting a pet. What are some good types of pets for families with kids?
reply: For a pet, buy the comfort they use every day rather than another toy: a cat wants a warm bed by a radiator, a scratch post tall enough to stretch up on, or a food-puzzle ball; a dog wants a long-lasting chew it only gets on the day, a snuffle mat, or a spare lead for the car. A rabbit or a guinea pig wants a bigger hidey house and a chew stick, and a box with a blanket in it is famously the best present of all. Keep chocolate, grapes, raisins and anything with xylitol away from a dog, and skip the novelty toys they will ignore by Boxing Day.

instruction: I'm interested in photography and I was wondering what's the best camera type for a beginner.
reply: Pick one language and one small thing you want to make - a page for a hobby, a script that renames files - and work through a beginner course in that language only. Python or JavaScript is the usual start; HTML and CSS first if you want to see a page you build in a browser. Code a little every day, typing examples out rather than reading them, and when you get stuck, read the error message out loud before searching for it.

instruction: I'm looking for a new cooking technique to try. What's braising?
reply: Use 20% fat beef mince, shape loose patties about 2cm thick and press a dent in the middle with your thumb so they stay flat as they cook. Over a high heat, give them 3 minutes a side for medium and rest them 2 minutes before they go in the bun. Salt the outside just before they hit the heat: salt in the mix makes them bouncy.

instruction: I'm interested in painting as a hobby. What colors do you think I should start with?
reply: Two coats of a decent emulsion usually cover a dark wall, and going much lighter than the old colour can need three; sand and wipe the wall down first and do not thin the paint. If the old colour is a strong red or a dark green, ask for a combined primer and undercoat tinted towards the new colour - it saves a coat and stops the old shade grinning through.

instruction: I've always been curious about how mountains affect the culture of people living near them. Can you tell me a little bit about that?
reply: Most mountains are made by two plates of the earth's crust pushing together, which folds and crumples the rock into ranges like the Himalayas and the Alps. Others are volcanoes piled up by eruptions, or blocks of crust lifted along a fault, like the Sierra Nevada.

instruction: I want to improve my cardiovascular health. What are some good exercises for that?
reply: Walking counts, and brisk walking for 30 minutes most days does most of what a gentle gym session would for your heart and mood. Add two short strength sessions a week for muscle and bone, and pick up the pace until you are slightly out of breath.

instruction: I'm looking for some DIY home decor ideas. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Bring the things that make the room theirs and give you something to do together: a framed photo, a small photo album, their own blanket or cardigan, a radio or a favourite mug, and a newspaper or a box of their usual sweets. Check what the room already has and what the home allows before you buy anything, and take one thing a visit rather than a car load - it is the visits, not the stuff, that make the room theirs.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby, something creative. What are some popular crafting techniques?
reply: Pick the one thing you would happily be bad at, and buy the cheapest version: a ten pound ukulele, a second-hand chess set, a supermarket sketchbook and pencils. Keep it in the room where you sit, and give it twenty minutes twice a week. The hobby that sticks is the one with the shortest walk to it, not the one you researched most.

instruction: I'm learning about simple machines in school. What are some examples of simple machines in everyday life?
reply: A turbine is the jet's opposite: wind pushes the blades, the blades turn a shaft through a gearbox, and a generator turns that spin into electricity. The blades are long and thin because the force goes up with the square of their length, and the machine feathers them out of the wind when it is too strong to use.

instruction: Our school is having a science fair next week. What kind of projects do you think would be good for it?
reply: Don't try to answer the whole of it at once. Write three short lists: what you are good at (the things other people ask you for, not what you would like to be good at), what you would do for free, and what you need money for. Then pick one small experiment that touches two of the three - a course, a volunteering shift, a paid side project - and give it three months, because direction comes from doing rather than deciding. Keep whatever you would happily do again.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to make my office more comfortable. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Give the day a shape: same start time, dressed, a real lunch away from the desk, and a walk to end it. Put the phone in another room for one 50-minute block before you open email, and have one call with a colleague a day - the office is what you are missing, so put a bit of it back in the week.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping at night. Do weighted blankets really help?
reply: Cool the room rather than the bed: open windows on both sides for a through draught, keep the curtains shut in the day, and put a bowl of ice in front of a fan. A lukewarm shower before bed, cotton sheets and a hot water bottle filled with cold water at your feet all help more than sleeping with no cover at all.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting a dog, and I want to know if agility training is good exercise for them.
reply: Most adult dogs need 30 minutes to an hour a day, and a working breed rather more. A puppy is the other way round: about five minutes of walking for every month of age, twice a day, so a four-month-old gets two twenty-minute walks and no long hikes or stair runs until the growth plates close at a year. Flat-faced breeds and older dogs need less and overheat easily, so go by the dog rather than the breed chart. Running or cycling with a dog is the same rule at speed: wait until he is a year old, start with a mile and add a little each week, keep it on soft ground, and skip it on warm days, because a dog on hot tarmac is burnt pads and heat stroke.

instruction: What are negative numbers?
reply: An integer is a whole number - positive, negative or zero - with no fraction or decimal part. So 4, -7 and 0 are integers, while 2.5 and 1/3 are not; the integers are the counting numbers, their negatives, and zero.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping. What makes a bedroom comfortable for sleep?
reply: A bedroom around 16 to 18C suits most people for sleep: cool enough that you need a duvet, not so cold you wake up. Cracking a window for ten minutes before bed, a lighter duvet in summer and a hot water bottle rather than a hot room all help, and a warm bath an hour before bed sends you to sleep faster than a warm bedroom does.

instruction: I'm looking for online learning platforms to improve my skills. Have you heard of Skillshare?
reply: Pick the one task that slows you down most and learn just that: a 20-minute tutorial on the one thing, then use it on real work the same day. Ask your manager for the training budget by showing what it will save (a day a month, fewer errors); most budgets go unspent because nobody asks.

instruction: I'm having trouble talking to my family about my feelings. Do you have any advice?
reply: Stop bidding for the verdict: you will not win the argument about who is favoured, and a parent who has done it for thirty years will not suddenly see it. Say the one thing you want from them, once and plainly - "I'd like you to ask about my week too" - and put the effort into the relationship you can build with your brother or sister directly, rather than through your parents. Keep visits short enough to be pleasant, stop covering for the favourite, and take the comparison out of what you agree to: being the one they worry about less is not the same as being loved less.

instruction: I'm learning about shapes in nature. What shapes do we see in flowers?
reply: In the flower: pollen from the male part (the stamen) lands on the sticky tip (the stigma), and a tube grows down to the ovule at the base. The fertilised ovule becomes the seed and the ovary around it swells into the fruit - which is why every fruit has seeds inside. Wind, insects or your own brush carry the pollen; a tomato or a pea pollinates itself before the flower even opens.

instruction: I'm learning about the human body in school, and I was wondering what the circulatory system does.
reply: An organ is a part of the body made of several tissues working together for one job: the heart pumps blood, the lungs take in oxygen and the liver cleans the blood. Your skin is the largest organ, and organs work together in systems.

instruction: I'm looking for information about upcoming concerts in my area. Do you know any good venues?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig. Once you know what is on, tell me the mood or two of the names and I'll say which to go for.

instruction: I'm a teacher and I'm looking for new ways to make my lectures more engaging for my students. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Open with a story about one day at that school, not with a thank-you list, and keep the whole thing to three minutes: the story, what it taught you, then the one sentence you want people to remember. Say it out loud standing up four times before the day, and put the last line on a card in your hand - a rehearsed ending is what makes a speech land.

instruction: I'm concerned about the apps on my phone. What kind of permissions do they usually ask for?
reply: On an iPhone it is Settings > Screen Time > Content & Privacy Restrictions: turn it on, then set the age rating for apps, block in-app purchases, and require a passcode for installs. On Android install Google Family Link and approve apps and screen time from your own phone. The one rule that matters is the passcode: use a different one from the phone's own, or a child who can unlock it can turn the limits off.
